n: A pilgrim looks up at the hills on the road to Jerusalem — beautiful, but also where robbers hid and pagan shrines stood. ‘Where does my help come from?’ is best read as a question.

f.w: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills

n: The answer: my help comes from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth — not from the hills, but from the One who made them.
A new voice, perhaps a fellow pilgrim or priest, reassures him: God won’t let your foot slip on the rocky path, and your guardian never dozes off.

f.w: will not suffer thy foot to be moved

n: The guardian of Israel never sleeps. Unlike pagan gods mocked for sleeping, Israel’s God is always awake.
The Lord is your keeper and your shade at your right side — like a protector walking beside you on the hot road.

f.g: Guardian, watchman — the key word of this psalm (six times).

n: No sunstroke by day, and no harm by night. The pair covers every hour of the journey.

f.w: The sun shall not smite thee

n: God will guard you from all harm and watch over your life.
He will guard your going out and coming in — every departure and return, all of life’s daily movement — now and forever.

f.w: thy going out and thy coming in
f.g: A Hebrew phrase for all of life’s activities.
